description:
Root-cause spike complete. The accumulated dirty prototype is evidence, not a landing candidate.

Goal
A source callable construction owns one runtime callable object and one producer-correlated member dispatch plan. Exact calls may bypass that object and use a private executable ABI. Every source CallClosure target, whether locally constructed or received generically, obeys the public callable ABI: boxed arguments, self, continuation; its result form is Absent, one boxed ValueRef, or Diverges.

First loss
Semantic analysis already preserves the correct authority in CallableFlowFact keyed by local producer: function, lexical captures, and each surface-to-resolution edge with capture and argument semantic mappings. Root backend packaging discards the producer boundary by flattening those edges into root-wide BackendCallableEntry rows, then asks one shared TransportPosition to choose a resolved_entry. A shared generic consumer legitimately receives multiple members, so no position-level entry stamp can represent the answer.

Runtime proof
Construction values already store a generated callable-boundary shim, not wrapper_fn. Zero-capture singletons and capturing closures both use the shim. The shim owns boxed args plus self plus cont, extracts captures, and tail-calls a private Direct wrapper. Exact closure calls bypass indirect CallClosure and retain narrow executable ABI.

The dirty spike makes interpreter member dispatch work but regresses previously-green native Range scalar and Range3. LLDB on the Enum.take crash proves the same return-seam error: fz_closure_get_capture_ref receives a runtime code address as continuation self because a one-word public result invoked a continuation compiled for two private result lanes plus self. Capture loading is the victim, not the source.

Authority model
- CallableFlowFact is the semantic authority for one producer construction and its member dispatch.
- The construction wrapper catalog owns producer, retained logical captures, member selection, semantic input mappings, and each member private input/return layout.
- TransportLayout is one component-solved fact containing structural shape plus physical carrier. Carrier is an independent monotone join, not a recursive post-hoc scan.
- The wrapper public return contract contains only Absent, BoxedValueRef, or Diverges. It does not copy a member structural ShapeId.
- Each member target owns its private return layout. One target-to-public adapter boxes it.
- CallReturnFlow owns public-to-caller delivery. Every indirect call uses one generic adapter; tail forwarding is allowed only when public and caller return forms agree.
- Construction identity is consumed at allocation to choose the shim. Once materialized, the runtime ValueRef code pointer and environment are the authority. Identity is not propagated beside the value.

Required implementation
1. Preserve producer-keyed construction facts from CallableFlowFact through root packaging. Generate one multi-member wrapper and dispatch plan per construction.
2. Materialize a first-class producer once with the construction shim and one ValueRef per retained logical capture. Exact direct-only values remain structural and allocation-free.
3. Make transport solve one TransportLayout per canonical component. Remove ExecutableRuntimeDemand.runtime_carriers, recursive transport_carrier_required, and duplicate position_shapes/transport_shapes storage rather than compensating for missing carrier propagation.
4. Replace wrapper return_layout chosen from the first nonempty member with a public return form. Keep private member return layouts only in the target-to-public adapter.
5. Make every indirect ClosureCall select its continuation adapter from the public return form, never from recovered construction identity or a target return position. Consolidate boxed Return and Deliver adapters.
6. Delete call-time construction repair: construction_wrapper_positions fixed-point propagation, BackendSemanticInputLayout.construction, RuntimeConstruction, native per-variable carried-boundary recovery, interpreter FnId/construction fallbacks used to choose return ABI, and target-derived closure return selection.
7. Encode allocation identity directly in MakeFnRef/MakeClosure or look it up by identity_fn; do not require NativeBody.callable_value_boundaries as a parallel per-variable authority. Unknown generic callables remain valid public-ABI values; opaque compiler callables remain ABI-conforming traps.
8. Remove the temporary FnId 16 eprintln/import before gates. Pare back prototype-only re-derivations rather than layering fixes over them.

Proof
- Model tests assert one producer construction with all members, stable member selection, one component TransportLayout, and no call-time identity side channel.
- Enum predicate/take/drop/split interp, JIT, run, and build.
- Range scalar, Range2 first accumulator, Range3 halt/suspend interp and JIT.
- Existing operator-ref reducer, opaque escaped lambda, continuation capture, spawn/destructor, and direct-only no-allocation contracts.
- cargo test --lib and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings.

Carrier proof
Range2 identified the exact first carrier loss without a special-case hypothesis. At the root callsite span 286..293, resume entry 1, value 3 has RuntimeDemand::Whole. Its solved component contains the selected executable return and the root ResumePayload, structural ShapeId 12, but both position branches hardcode carrier false, so the final layout is Absent. Component-wide joining cannot repair false seeds. Carrier must be projected from the authoritative demand of every component member, then joined once; result/return/resume position kinds do not define carrier semantics.

Public return seam proof
The remaining Range2 trace proved that private member return and public callable return are currently invalidly equated before native lowering. jobs/artifact.rs call_return_flow treats a ClosureCall target hint as CallTarget::Local(member): Deliver names the member ExecutableReturn as payload, and Return compares that member return against caller payload/return to classify Tail. Backend preserves this flow even when runtime invocation is indirect and member selection belongs to the construction wrapper. A private member return such as RawAtom plus ValueRef and the public boxed ValueRef result therefore enter one transport component; broad carrier joins only move the mismatch. Construction closure calls need an explicit public callable-return source/layout keyed by their boundary or callsite. Member target-to-public adaptation ends at that seam; public-to-caller adaptation begins there. Only exact direct closure calls may use member ExecutableReturn and its tail equality.

Carrier authority correction
The first direct-demand carrier redesign was falsified. Non-Ignore RuntimeDemand means the semantic value is live; it does not mean the private ABI is boxed. Structural shape already supplies private lanes. Treating every demanded ExecutableReturn as ValueRef caused wrapper target-to-public adaptation to reinterpret raw member values as tagged boxes, producing Nil. Carrier must be an explicit physical seam anchor joined through the transport component: first-class callable publication/materialization and the public callable return seam anchor ValueRef; ordinary private executable returns and direct values remain structural unless their own boundary anchors otherwise. Resume/Return payloads inherit public boxing only through equality with the public seam, never from position kind or generic liveness.

Exact-call return proof
Range2 LLDB proves the first malformed handoff is Fn2 -> Fn56: Fn2 returns private RawInt 3, while Fn56 declares ValueRef. Fn56 and Fn99 preserve raw 3 as if boxed; Fn92 later calls fz_unbox_int(0x3) and observes Nil. The runtime callable is correct: Fn39 MakeFnRef(Fn35) resolves construction 0 to generated boundary 0 and callable_wrapper_0 Fn37. Tuple projection, tuple_field_params, stale-GC, construction selection, and public-wrapper-return hypotheses were falsified.
The bad edge is an exact closure-call fast path inside the wrapper member. Native lowering correctly knows the exact private target but closure_call_return_position deliberately returns None whenever construction identity is present. delivered_call_continuation then falls back to the public ResumePayload and creates a ValueRef continuation instead of decoding the exact target ExecutableReturn RawInt and adapting it to the public payload. Construction identity is therefore being used at call time to suppress the private source ABI, contradicting the model that identity is consumed only at allocation.
Implementation must remove this call-time construction-dependent return selection. An exact direct closure call always takes its source contract from the exact target ExecutableReturn; its continuation adapts that private result to the public payload/caller contract. Indirect calls remain public ABI. Remove the redundant construction parameter/branch rather than adding a boxing fallback or changing Fn56/Fn92. Tail forwarding remains legal only for physically identical private/caller contracts.

CallReturnFlow authority proof
The Fn55 -> Fn2 Range2 edge falsified construction-dependent closure-return repair as the first authority. Artifact call_return_flow already knows direct local Fn2 ExecutableReturn RawInt and waits for its transport layout, but Continue drops that source and retains only ReturnPayload ValueRef. Native emit_native_direct_call_tail consumes Continue through return_lane_continuation_for_payload, creating Fn56 ValueRef; Fn2 writes raw 3, which reaches Fn99 as Nil. The minimal model is one mandatory source TransportPosition on every CallReturnFlow variant: direct local source is callee ExecutableReturn; public/indirect source is the public payload seam; Tail records source plus caller return and is legal only when their physical contracts agree; Deliver records source plus public payload/resume. Native lowers source-to-payload exactly once. This removes closure_call_return_position, source_return Option plumbing, and call-time construction selection rather than adding a boxing fallback.

Route-model spike
The first implementation falsified the assumption that TransportLayout is a complete tail contract. It contains only structural ShapeId plus Absent/ValueRef carrier; it does not represent the raw ABI lane representations selected by CodegenSeam. Comparing source, ReturnPayload, and caller TransportLayout therefore classified Enum.reduce private edges as Tail while their physical return seams differ. Backend interp then reaches executable 8/function 159/entry 1 with compiler2_unreachable_control, and native JIT returns 7 instead of 15. The fixture produced no public=true route: its first break is before native lowering. Do not repair this in Native. Canonical route layout must include the physical lane contract, or Tail must ask the existing canonical seam contract directly.

Construction identity remains required at callable allocation/materialization to select the producer wrapper; removing it there changes Enum.reduce from 15 to 7. It is not return-flow authority. The unresolved distinction is explicit in the route model: exact devirtualized closure calls source the target ExecutableReturn; runtime indirect closure calls source the construction public seam. Artifact materialization must record that route kind instead of inferring public/private from a construction lookup in Native.

Physical-contract inventory
Position layouts hold only structural ShapeId plus Absent/ValueRef carrier. Codegen seam facts own raw lane reprs, but jobs/backend generates them after artifact call-return flow has already sealed CallReturnFlow; an artifact-stage probe found no matching seam facts. Native then scans the later seam facts to rederive every return contract. Neither position layout nor codegen seam can be route authority at the current lifecycle.

The physical contracts already have correct owners: every BackendExecutable return layout is the private target return, and every BackendConstructionWrapper return layout is the public callable ABI. Make those layouts available when routes are sealed. A route must carry contract-bearing endpoints, not only positions: Exact target/private return for a devirtualized closure, Public construction/public return for a runtime ClosureCall, plus the caller sink contract. Tail is constructible only when complete endpoint return layouts are equal. Continue and Deliver carry source and sink layouts so Native consumes them directly and deletes native-return-contract seam scans and position-derived ABI fallbacks.

Route-kind proof
Artifact can distinguish the cases without construction as return authority. materialize-transport-closure-call-edge yields a single exact resolution and packages CallEdge Direct; backend preserves BackendTail ClosureCall target Some. Its source is the selected executable private return layout. Without an exact resolution, artifact produces CallEdge Indirect or no direct edge; backend packages target None. Its source is the callable construction public return layout, selected at allocation by producer identity. Native receives route kind and layout and never inspects construction to choose source ABI. The current design leaves return flow None for that latter case, which is the missing model field.

Backend sealing point
Root backend packaging already has the complete ABI inventory before it packages symbolic tails: every reachable symbolic backend executable carries AbiReadyExecutable return_layout, and package-backend-construction-wrappers has created each public wrapper return_layout. It also owns the final MaterializedTransportPlan and its codegen seam facts. This is the only coherent sealing point. Artifact retains a symbolic route intent and never classifies Tail. Backend packaging resolves exact target indexes and construction identities, materializes one physical endpoint layout for source and sink, and emits BackendReturnFlow consumed by both backend interpreter and Native. ReturnPayload and ResumePayload sink layouts must be materialized there once from their owner seam facts and stored on the route; no Native scan remains. This is not a semantic TransportLayout extension and does not duplicate ABI derivation: it closes the existing backend handoff product.

Semantic runtime-domain proof
Enum reachability failure is upstream of return routing. e8/f159 calls exact f65 and executes a returned Int(1), but f65 ReturnType is absent, so its delivered resume is pruned. The canonical f65 body receives activation-input evidence displayed as bare templates a0 and a1 and tail-calls Kernel.+/2. calculate_dispatch_reachability treats those variables as concrete non-overlapping subjects, produces no dispatch outcomes, and only marks failure reachable. The absence propagates back through f65 and f159 even though runtime values are integers.
A type inference template is not a runtime subject domain. Dispatch reachability must consume a grounded runtime envelope: replace free variables with Any recursively while preserving known surrounding list/tuple/callable structure, then refine that envelope along dispatch proofs. For a0+a1 this yields integer/float outcomes and ground arm inputs rather than pruning the call. Mapping only a top-level variable, manufacturing return evidence from a contract, or marking the dead resume reachable would be compensations. This is the purpose served by a known-subject-domain conversion: separate symbolic inference identity from the runtime value set used for dispatch.

Range3 native proof
The first failing adapter is return_lanes__73_13. Its source is FunctionId 75 ExecutableReturn with native seam repr [ValueRef]; its caller body Fn73 declares return reprs [RawAtom, RawInt]. Native return_lane_continuation_for_source_payload decodes the source correctly, then encodes to ReturnPayload and emits that one payload lane as ReturnLanes. Codegen rejects lanes=1 against return_reprs=2. The sealed source is not wrong: the adapter incorrectly treats payload as the final sink. Continue must carry and Native must encode to the sealed caller-return endpoint after any payload/resume adaptation, or payload must be a separate consumed stage. This is the same forbidden payload-as-source/final-sink conflation, not a CodegenSeam disagreement.

Range2 continuation proof
After Continue was retargeted to caller_return, Range2 native lowering first fails in Continuation owner Fn93 index19: native attempted to materialize Absent as runtime Ty21. This is before codegen and differs from Range3. The source-to-caller direct conversion exposes a semantic gap: this route needs its ReturnPayload stage to construct a value required by the caller contract; payload is neither the source ABI nor an ignorable final sink. The correct model must represent payload as an explicit adaptation stage when it is consumed, rather than replacing it universally with caller_return. No fallback or lane padding is valid.

Range2 staged-value proof
Fn93/index19 receives FunctionId130 ExecutableReturn with source ShapeId15, zero source reprs, and decoded NativeBoundValue Absent. Its owner FunctionId129 caller-return is ShapeId11 with [RawInt]. Thus this is not a raw-versus-boxed disagreement: ReturnPayload is the first-accumulator bridge that constructs the caller logical integer from a zero-width private result. Direct source-to-caller encode must fail because Absent has no integer materialization. The correct route model needs an explicit payload transformation stage for this edge; source->payload produces the bridge value and payload->caller carries its final ABI. The stage should be represented by the destination/control continuation, not an intermediate runtime allocation.

Range2 backend-tail proof
Backend Function129 is a one-clause tuple-state dispatcher: it projects its sole tuple input then DirectCall-dispatches callsite 0 with destination Return. Dispatch arm body0 selects local executable 30, Function130 arrow Ty160 input Ty56, with Continue source Function130 ExecutableReturn and caller Function129 ExecutableReturn. Its source layout is zero-width; arm body1 selects a different Function130 activation and is Tail. The first-accumulator transformation is therefore not a DeliveredResume entry or Fn93 capture: it belongs to the dispatch outcome selected by the Function129 state tuple. Fn93 is a generic return adapter incorrectly attached to the body0 zero-result arm as if it directly produced Function129 final return. The existing dispatch plan distinguishes first state in its arm bodies; packaging must preserve that control outcome as the payload transformation stage before a final caller-return adapter.

Range2 divergence proof
The selected Function130 activation arrow Ty160 has return_ty none, Types::is_empty true, effects.halts true, and its only tail calls Enum.EmptyError with Tail. It is divergent and legitimately has zero return lanes. A separate Function130 activation returns int, proving FunctionId alone is insufficient. Fn129 dispatch arm body0 selected the divergent Ty160 activation but CallReturnFlow became Continue because BackendReturnLayout records only structural and reprs, not divergence. This is the first mismatch. Canonical BackendReturnLayout needs a Diverges bit derived once from each executable return_ty (and wrapper member/public return contracts); package-time sealing must retain Tail when source diverges regardless of sink layout. Native must emit no adapter for this route.

Direct-only authority proof
The runtime-envelope repair exposed a separate prototype compensation. Runtime demand had been changed to walk every clause of every multi-clause body. In the direct-only Enum.reduce fixture, Function179 has an unreachable reducer ClosureCall whose CallSiteSummary is intentionally absent. Walking it anyway calls closure_callee_demand(None), manufactures opaque=true, propagates that false uncertainty through Function166, and publishes two boundaries for the otherwise direct bridge producer. Restoring the authoritative reachable_clauses walk plus the existing narrowly-proven trivial-value delta removes every boundary: both callable facts have boundary_ids=[], both producer layouts are carrier Absent, and no first-class publication exists. Semantic reachability, not structural codegen coverage, owns runtime demand.

After removing that pollution, the actual reducer invocation in Function179 remains BackendTail::ClosureCall target=Some with construction=None. Producer correlation therefore survives to the call and the private exact ABI is authoritative; no runtime callable object is needed. The remaining Native failure occurs earlier while the reducer transits a Dispatch direct-call edge. lower_dispatch_call_tail eagerly materializes every semantic argument before evaluating the dispatch plan, although the plan discriminates only on list/state and the selected arm later encodes arguments from its own target input layouts. The reducer is nondiscriminating, has RuntimeDemand shape Ignore with concrete resolved surfaces and opaque=false/escape=false, and carries zero lanes. Eagerly materializing it invents a boxed-runtime obligation and fails on its zero-lane callable shape. Dispatch evaluation must consume only graph-required inputs; arm ABI encoding remains the sole authority for forwarded arguments.

Inventory proof
BackendCallableEntry has no consumers outside backend packaging and the BackendProgram field. package_backend_callable_entries emits one row for every CallableFacts resolution even when boundary_ids is empty, which is why the direct-only backend inventory is nonempty. A public callable entry can only be justified by an actual BoundaryId publication; direct targets already live in executable call edges. The producer construction catalog is semantic correlation and may contain direct-only producers, but BackendConstructionWrapper/native callable boundaries are runtime objects and must be materialized only for producer positions with a proven public publication. Filtering after Native would be a compensation; packaging must distinguish semantic construction facts from published runtime constructions at the backend boundary.

Published-construction positive control
The enum_predicate_search positive fixture contains both direct-only root producers and genuinely public internal producers. Every public producer has one or more MaterializedTransportPlan.publication_boundaries rows whose position equals the construction producer; the direct-only root producers have none. This holds even when several activations share a CallableId. Therefore the producer position is the complete runtime-materialization gate already present in the model: semantic CallableConstructionFact may exist for direct correlation, but BackendConstructionWrapper exists iff its producer position is published. No callable-id filter, downstream scan, or Native recovery is needed.

Range construction proof
The all-multi-clause demand walk was compensating for two consumer/model errors, not missing semantic reachability. Range3 produces separate grounded Range.reduce activations: {:cont, int} reaches clause 1 and {:suspend, int} reaches clause 3. The suspension closure producer Function69/Value34 is correctly published at BoundaryId(2), has zero in-program members, and must still materialize as a public-ABI callable. Its producer-owned wrapper is an ABI-conforming function_clause trap. It needs no retained captures because no member consumes them. Empty members therefore do not mean no runtime object; publication is the gate.

The scalar Function67 bridge producers have members but boundary_ids=[] and no producer publications. Their eventual ClosureCall is exact, so they stay structural and need no wrapper. Their reducer capture shape is zero-width; both member target layouts correctly record that capture semantic input with reprs=[]. The interpreter failure comes from reading every logical source capture before checking physical width. Direct structural construction must skip zero-width captures.

Capture projection proof
BackendConstructionWrapper.captures is a logical capture map with a carrier per slot. Native already stores only ValueRef slots in the runtime closure. The backend interpreter instead requires physical capture count == logical slot count and zips them positionally, causing unbound direct captures and misaligned semantic arguments. Both consumers must project the same way: source capture lists and member capture_semantic_inputs retain logical length; runtime environments contain only slots whose carrier is ValueRef; absent slots map to target semantic inputs whose reprs are empty and require no value. Arguments map only through surface_semantic_inputs, never by filling every remaining semantic slot in ordinal order.

Final wrapper gate
A BackendConstructionWrapper exists iff the producer position has a publication boundary, regardless of member count. Published zero-member constructions lower to a public-ABI trap. Unpublished constructions remain only semantic correlation facts for exact private calls. This replaces both package-all and filter-nonempty rules.

Entry-capture physical contract proof
Range scalar Function75 entry3 logically captures semantic value0, but its demand and downstream target input are both Ignore/reprs=[]. The settled EntryCapture TransportLayout is structural ShapeId12 (an int Lane) with carrier Absent. Backend interpreter position_is_runtime_absent checks only ShapeDescr::Nothing and therefore reads an intentionally unbound capture. Structural width would also be wrong: private raw-lane presence is owned by the codegen seam contract, not TransportLayout. Native currently rescans seam facts in entry_capture_reprs, duplicating that derivation. Backend packaging must seal each entry capture as one record containing value, position, structural shape, and physical reprs. Interpreter and Native consume the record directly; remove parallel captures/capture_positions and the Native seam scan.

Entry-capture seam identity proof
Gating ignored capture emission still left Function75 capture0 as RawInt because CodegenSeam::BlockParam identifies only (executable, entry). Another demanded int capture in the same entry emits the same (shape,lane), so lookup aliases its fact onto capture0. The codegen seam key has lost the capture slot. Add CodegenSeam::EntryCapture { executable, entry, capture_index }; structural and publication facts for TransportPosition::EntryCapture use it, and BackendEntryCapture sealing matches it exactly. BlockParam remains the owner for resume payload/block-param lanes. This removes cross-capture aliasing rather than adding demand checks at consumers.

Exact zero-width callee proof
Range scalar Function75 entry3 has six logical captures and a sealed physical contract of four RawInt lanes: capture0 and callable capture5 both have tys=[]/reprs=[]. Native entry binding correctly consumes four lanes, but replaces every zero-width capture with NativeBoundValue::Absent. The entry then executes an exact ClosureCall with target executable26, construction=None, two surface args, and no physical capture inputs. Backend interpreter succeeds because an unavailable exact callee is legal when every target capture input has reprs=[]; it takes the exact target and supplies zero capture lanes. Native instead requires the callee value to be a shape-bearing Transport before taking its exact fast path. Absent loses that shape, so Native falls into public materialization and fails.

The authority is the exact call edge plus the target's sealed semantic input layouts, not a runtime callee object. For target=Some and construction=None, Native must validate the target capture prefix: unavailable/zero-width callee is valid iff every capture input reprs is empty; otherwise it is an error. It then encodes only the target's physical argument inputs. This is the same rule already proven by the backend interpreter and avoids preserving an artificial runtime value or reconstructing construction identity. Indirect calls still require the public callable value.
title: fz-k22: preserve producer callable constructions behind one public indirect ABI
